purpose: Auditable ledger of the Local2 P0 closure. Every entry is falsifiable: commit SHAs are checked against the repository, test counts against a re-run, and statuses against the vocabulary in section 21 of the closure spec.

phases.title: Read/Search Navigation
evidence: file.read gains start_line and a hard 8000-line ceiling enforced identically on both dispatch paths
file.search gains max_results, context_before/after and deterministic ordering via rg --sort path
the fast path previously passed max_lines straight to the renderer, so max_lines=1e7 returned the whole file on one path and 8000 lines on the other

phases.title: Test/Build Execution
evidence: ExecutionFailureClass.TEST_SUITE_FAILED separates a tool reporting a verdict from a process misbehaving, scoped by tool rather than by exit code
test.run no longer infers the runner from what is installed; the fallback is gated on project ecosystem markers and otherwise fails closed
declared runtime versus actual runtime is an execution admission gate; ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH refuses with no execution_id

phases.title: Process Lifecycle
evidence: stdout_truncated and stderr_truncated now travel from direct_exec into ExecutionRecord and to_public; previously the flags were computed and discarded
is_terminal is exposed so callers need not hardcode the terminal set
START to RUNNING to COMPLETE, FAILED and CANCELLED are each observed on a real subprocess

findings.summary: A cancel issued while an execution is still STARTING returns ok=true and leaves the command running to COMPLETED, because there is no process group to signal yet.
findings.why_open: Cancelling after RUNNING does reach CANCELLED, which P0-H qualifies. The pre-RUNNING window is unproven and is a lifecycle question, not a WIP one.
findings.evidence: veya/remote/execution.py cancel(): os.killpg is guarded by if record.process_group_id

phases.title: Security / Permission / Sandbox
evidence: five escape routes refused with no execution_id and no tool reached: parent traversal, /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ, a sibling directory, and a symlink pointing outside
UNKNOWN resolves to UNKNOWN and is refused at the tool boundary with TOOL_DENIED; it is deliberately outside EFFECT_LATTICE
the four authorities hold none of each other's verdicts

phases.title: WIP Preservation
evidence: a governed file.write lands under .veya/worktrees/ and the canonical file is never created
staged index, unstaged set, untracked files, HEAD and branch survive a write, a refusal, a failing execution and a cancel
session-level content-hash comparison: every tracked modification and all 13 untracked files byte-identical across the phase

findings.summary: Spec 10.3 asks for an isolated worktree by default for tests. On main that holds for mutation only: read and execute intent default to CANONICAL_WORKTREE, so a command that writes writes into the owner's live tree.
findings.why_open: The resolver documents the reason, and it is defensible: a fresh worktree is a clean checkout with no virtualenv and none of the current working state, so running there made the tree's own modules unimportable. This is a spec-versus-implementation divergence and an architecture decision, escalated rather than accepted or fixed.
findings.evidence: veya/remote/tool_adapter.py resolve_execution_target rule 4 and its comment; measured by tests/remote/test_p0j_wip_preservation.py::test_a_writing_command_pollutes_the_canonical_tree

blockers.summary: runtime.coding.tools.coding_worktree_create fails in this environment with: module 'oskill' has no attribute 'capability_intersection'.
blockers.workaround: WorktreeManager is used directly so the adapter's isolation and identity verification remain under test.
blockers.owner: harness work already in flight in the working tree

phases.title: Full Local Development E2E
evidence: The explicit isolated-execution gate WORKS: test.run with execution_target=NEW_ISOLATED_WORKTREE reports target_type NEW_ISOLATED_WORKTREE, executes with cwd set to .veya/worktrees/task-*, and the command's own os.getcwd() independently matches the record's cwd.
Canonical HEAD, the modified tracked file and canonical source contents were all byte-identical across that run, so P0-J-F1 has a working remedy available even though the default stays canonical.
The sequence cannot be carried past the repair step because main has no commit surface: the git.* tools are git.status, git.diff, git.log and git.promote only.
veya/remote/git_promotion.py states 'Promotion != Commit: changes remain in working tree/index; NO auto-commit, NO auto-push', and git.promote requires an execution_id whose commit already exists.

blockers.summary: No git.stage and no git.commit exist in the governed surface, so acceptance steps 13-18 (stage, commit, verify commit, promote) cannot be executed.
blockers.why_blocked: The only route would be shell.exec running git add/git commit, which is the bypass the closure spec forbids, or adding a commit capability, which is an architecture change rather than a qualification.
blockers.evidence: BINDINGS git.* == [git.status, git.diff, git.log, git.promote]; runtime/coding has no coding_*commit* function
blockers.owner: requires an architecture decision before P0-L can run

phases.title: Full Local Development E2E (rerun)
evidence: Steps A-M are reachable on the governed surface: the explicit NEW_ISOLATED_WORKTREE target resolves, file.read/file.search are bounded against it, file.write lands in the worktree, test.run produces a real TEST_SUITE_FAILED then a real pass after a governed repair, build.run runs for real, and git.stage/git.commit produce a commit whose SHA matches an independent git rev-parse.
git.stage and git.commit are bound to coding_git_stage and coding_git_commit and route through WorktreeManager, so P0-M's authority topology holds.
Canonical HEAD, branch and tracked file contents are unchanged throughout, so WIP preservation holds.

git.verify does not exist in the governed surface (git.* is status, diff, stage, commit, log, promote) and P0-M did not add it, so the verify step named by the rerun spec has no governed implementation.

blockers.summary: Step M (Git Verify) names git.verify, which does not exist as a governed tool. Adding it is outside the rerun's permitted change set.
blockers.why_blocked: Section 46 freezes the governed git surface. Verification could only be done with the git CLI as an independent oracle, which is a reinterpretation of the spec rather than the spec's letter.
blockers.evidence: BINDINGS git.* == [git.status, git.diff, git.stage, git.commit, git.log, git.promote]

blockers.summary: Sections 24 and 25 require the whole lifecycle to belong to one durable GoalRun and to end in a Verifier ACCEPT, but the governed tools this rerun must use are direct RemoteToolAdapter jobs with no Verifier.
blockers.why_blocked: ExecutionRecord carries goal_run_id and task_id but has no verifier field at all, and the direct command flow does not populate a GoalRun. The only GoalRun-attached governed path is worker.dispatch, which requires an LLM worker binary and is unavailable here. Wiring a Verifier into the direct path is outside the permitted change set.
blockers.evidence: ExecutionRecord has no field matching 'verif'; set_effect_receipt/EffectReceipt is reached only from worker.dispatch

blockers.summary: Section 23 makes a structured-receipt defect a BLOCKED condition, and TOOL-BUG-1 is still open.
blockers.why_blocked: set_finalization_evidence still assigns record.effect_receipt only when isinstance(receipt, dict), with no else branch, so a stringified receipt is silently discarded. Section 3.6 forbids fixing it in this phase.

phases.title: Governed git.verify
evidence: git.verify is bound to a new coding_git_verify canonical tool and routes through WorktreeManager.verify, the same authority git.stage and git.commit use. It is a READ and creates no commit.

Verified through the gateway, not only at the manager: file.write -> git.stage -> git.commit -> git.verify on an explicit NEW_ISOLATED_WORKTREE, with the resulting SHA, parent, tree and changed paths each cross-checked against the git CLI used purely as an oracle.

Fails closed. A SHA absent from this repository, an empty or too-short name, a commit belonging to another repository, a changed-path set differing from the declared one, a canonical target, and an unregistered directory are all refused with POLICY_BLOCKED at the gateway.

BINDINGS moved 44 -> 45. The three recorded count guards (P0-F, P0-M, supervision sentinel) were restated with the reason rather than relaxed, and the P0-M guard additionally pins the full git.* name set so a later addition cannot quietly satisfy it.
git.promote is untouched: the guard still asserts 'Promotion != Commit' and 'NO auto-commit, NO auto-push', and git.verify is not routed to it.

Regression is unchanged against the recorded baseline: P0-F..N plus security 176 passed, unit-fast 406 passed, goalrun 1 failed / 200 passed, runtime 23 failed / 506 passed. The goalrun and runtime failures are the same ones recorded before this phase.
The 12 test_direct_fast_path failures were reproduced identically in a detached worktree at b424e00a, so they predate this phase and are not caused by it.
notes: Ref expressions are refused rather than raised: a caller passing HEAD or sha~1 gets verified=false with the resolved SHA reported, so a moving target cannot be reported as a verified commit. Verified by mutation M4.

M4 and M7 initially survived the first mutation attempt. Both were coverage gaps in the tests, not defects hidden by the implementation, and were closed by deepening the fixture and pinning the ref case; both are now RED under mutation. M5 initially went RED for the wrong reason (a corrupted tree expression rather than the removed guard), which is why the two unreachable emptiness guards were deleted instead of kept.

A separate pre-existing failure is reported and not fixed: tests/server/test_coding_tools.py asserts a 13-tool count that has been stale since P0-M (14 then 15), and that file is in no required CI suite, which is why it went unnoticed. It is out of scope here and is recorded for a separate phase.

phases.title: Direct-path GoalRun / Verifier architecture decision

audit_answers.q1_direct_associates_goal_run: YES, verified at runtime. A gateway test.run produced goal_run_id='goal_20261005_144316_15128cb02366' and goal_task_id='remote:direct_...'. The field is empty at construction and populated later by RemoteGoalRunAdapter.before_execution (veya/remote/execution.py:2775).
audit_answers.q2_who_assigns_goal_run_id: RemoteGoalRunAdapter.before_execution, from state.goal_id (veya/remote/execution.py:2775). goal_task_id is defaulted at execution.py:2948 as f'remote:{execution_id}'.
audit_answers.q3_canonical_verifier_authority: Exactly one: CanonicalWorkerAdapter.finalize_candidate (server/goal_run/canonical_worker.py:586), which collects an EvidenceBundle and calls VerificationEngine.run_independent_verifier.
audit_answers.q4_who_consumes_accept: server/goal_run/runner.py:2097, guarded by hasattr(integration_adapter, 'finalize_candidate'). RemoteGoalRunAdapter does not implement it, so the branch is skipped and the verdict is never produced.
audit_answers.q5_goalrun_complete_authority: _decide_goal_completion (server/goal_run/runner.py:1548) is the single decider of state.status.
audit_answers.q6_second_completion_authority: Two terminal authorities already coexist and always did: ExecutionRecord._finish (veya/remote/execution.py:3095) and _decide_goal_completion. This is pre-existing, is not introduced by B, and was not touched by P0-N. Recorded as an open observation, not a P0-O blocker.
audit_answers.q7_is_worker_dispatch_the_sole_entry: NO. _admit_goal_run is invoked from both submit (veya/remote/execution.py:2067) and recovery (:1615). test.run, build.run and shell.exec already traverse project_run_goal.
audit_answers.q8_can_direct_be_execution_attempts: Already true de facto for _COMMAND_TOOLS (shell.exec, test.run, build.run) via RemoteGoalRunAdapter.execute_semantic_task -> runner(reporter).
audit_answers.q9_why_worker_dispatch_needs_an_llm: worker.dispatch requires worker in _WORKER_TYPES, which is ExecutorRegistry membership; every admitted executor is an LLM runtime. This is a property of worker.dispatch, not of GoalRun.
audit_answers.q10_would_direct_force_provider_dependen: NO. execute_semantic_task calls runner(reporter) only. g1_plan consumes explicit_tasks with skip_plan_review=True, and skip_advisory_code_review=True is set on the adapter. No model call occurs on this path. P0-L needed an LLM only because it chose worker.dispatch.

phases.state_transition_map: submit(execution_type=DIRECT) -> PERSISTED -> _admit_goal_run -> project_run_goal(state=running) -> before_execution(RUNNING/EDITING) -> execute_semantic_task -> _finish(COMPLETED|FAILED|CANCELLED) -> reconcile_task (:2698-2713) -> _decide_goal_completion -> state.status

ownership.receipt: ExecutionRecord + EffectReceipt. TOOL-BUG-1 is a receipt-serialization defect, not an architecture concern, and stays separate as SF-RECEIPT.
ownership.verifier: VerificationEngine, reachable only through finalize_candidate; currently unreachable from the direct path.
ownership.goalrun_lineage: Already established: goal_run_id + goal_task_id + reconcile_task projection.
ownership.git_surface: The git.* fast path (_call_fast_git, veya/remote/tool_adapter.py:4364) creates no ExecutionRecord, no GoalRun, no receipt and no verifier. P0-N evidence is self-contained by design.

correction.subject: P0-L attempt 2 (b424e00a) rationale
correction.incorrect_conclusion: The direct governed command path has no GoalRun attachment and no Verifier capability, so satisfying closure spec sections 24 and 25 would require an architecture extension outside the phase's permitted change set.
correction.why_incorrect: It was inferred from construction-time ExecutionRecord state. goal_run_id is None when the record is created and is assigned by RemoteGoalRunAdapter.before_execution once the run is admitted, so a static read of the dataclass fields at the wrong moment reported absence that does not exist at runtime.
correction.corrected_conclusion: Direct execution is already GoalRun-backed, the GoalRun terminal authority already exists, and reconcile_task already exists. The single actual gap is that RemoteGoalRunAdapter declares verification_required=True but does not implement finalize_candidate, which leaves canonical_acceptance_deferred as a fail-open acceptance.
correction.scope_of_correction: This corrects the rationale only. The P0-L attempt 2 verdict of BLOCKED still stood under the spec in force at b424e00a, because sections 24 and 25 were demonstrably unmet at af3e5f12. The recorded verdict is not rewritten and no historical entry is altered or removed; f5af9744 (attempt 1) and b424e00a (attempt 2) both remain BLOCKED.

actual_gap.summary: RemoteGoalRunAdapter sets verification_required=True but implements no finalize_candidate, so runner.py:666-677 marks the task passed=True with reason 'canonical_acceptance_deferred' and the deferral target is never invoked. Acceptance is assumed rather than verified on the direct development path.
actual_gap.scope: one method on one adapter; the VerificationEngine and the GoalRun terminal authority already exist

next_phase.title: Direct-path verifier integration
next_phase.must_prove_failure: direct test.run FAIL -> ExecutionRecord FAILED -> reconcile_task -> GoalRun RECOVERING, explicitly NOT COMPLETED
next_phase.must_prove_success: direct test.run PASS -> VerificationEngine -> ACCEPT -> GoalRun COMPLETE

separate_finding.summary: The git.* fast path has no ExecutionRecord, no GoalRun, no receipt and no verifier, so the git surface and the direct execution surface have inconsistent lifecycle models.
separate_finding.deferral: Decide in a future dedicated Git lifecycle phase whether git operations require ExecutionRecord / GoalRun / receipt participation. Explicitly NOT in P0-P scope; the git surface keeps its current responsibility (git.stage, git.commit, git.verify, git.promote).

evidence: Runtime observation through the governed gateway: a real test.run on an explicit workspace produced execution_type='direct', goal_run_id='goal_20261005_144316_15128cb02366' and goal_task_id='remote:direct_4dae1f6408b64ddb96099035dfdb4aec', with dispatch_id=None. Direct execution therefore already carries GoalRun lineage, which corrects the P0-L attempt 2 rationale that inferred its absence from construction-time record state.

Static authority trace: _admit_goal_run is reached from submit (veya/remote/execution.py:2067) and from recovery (:1615), so worker.dispatch is not the sole entry into project_run_goal; the three _COMMAND_TOOLS already traverse the same GoalRun runner that the worker path uses.

Verifier authority is singular: CanonicalWorkerAdapter.finalize_candidate (server/goal_run/canonical_worker.py:586) is the only implementation, and runner.py:2097 gates acceptance on hasattr(integration_adapter, 'finalize_candidate'). An AST scan of RemoteGoalRunAdapter confirms it defines before_execution, before_iteration, checkpoint and execute_semantic_task but not finalize_candidate.

No provider dependency is required on this path: execute_semantic_task invokes runner(reporter) only, and g1_plan consumes explicit_tasks with skip_plan_review=True while the adapter sets skip_advisory_code_review=True. The LLM requirement observed in P0-L belongs to worker.dispatch's ExecutorRegistry membership check, not to GoalRun.

The resulting gap is bounded and fail-open: runner.py:666-677 assigns passed=True with reason 'canonical_acceptance_deferred' whenever an adapter declares verification_required without implementing finalize_candidate, and RemoteGoalRunAdapter sets verification_required=True at veya/remote/execution.py:2767 while implementing no verifier, so acceptance is assumed rather than earned.

The audit was read-only: no source file, no TargetContract, no default execution target, no WorktreeManager, no git.promote and no P0-L entry was modified. P0-L attempt 1 (f5af9744) and attempt 2 (b424e00a) both remain recorded as BLOCKED and were neither rewritten nor removed.

target_contract.reason: TargetContract does not exist on main. It is present only on local2/l0-l1-l2. Per spec section 3 no phase may claim convergence, and redoing P0-B/P0-E on main is forbidden.

tool_bug_1.summary: A non-dict effect receipt is silently discarded rather than rejected, so a receipt that arrives stringified is indistinguishable from no receipt at all.
tool_bug_1.evidence: veya/remote/execution.py set_finalization_evidence assigns record.effect_receipt only when isinstance(receipt, dict); there is no else branch and no diagnostic.
tool_bug_1.why_not_closed: Fixing it changes finalizer evidence handling on a governed path and needs its own qualification. Closing it by asserting the schema would be exactly the fake evidence this phase exists to prevent.

mutations_green_then_repaired.cause: the containment check had no test anywhere in the suite
mutations_green_then_repaired.repair: added two negative tests plus a positive counter-test, re-ran RED

mutations_green_then_repaired.cause: every assertion was made against a record that genuinely was terminal
mutations_green_then_repaired.repair: asserted is_terminal is False on an observed running record, re-ran RED

baseline_failures_untouched.note: Isolated per spec section 24 and not re-baselined. runtime 24 failed / 505 passed and goalrun 1 failed / 200 passed have failure sets byte-identical to the pre-P0 measurement.

closure_gate.reason: P0-O decided the architecture (B) and showed the direct path is already GoalRun-backed, reducing the remaining work to one verification seam (P0-P). P0-L still cannot PASS while P0-O-G1 leaves acceptance fail-open and while TOOL-BUG-1 (SF-RECEIPT) leaves receipt serialization able to drop a non-dict receipt silently. Local2 local development closure cannot be declared COMPLETE. Integration remains deferred.

wip_preservation.method: content-hash comparison before and after every phase
wip_preservation.forbidden_operations_used: none: no git clean, no git reset, no git stash at any point in P0-F through P0-K
